title: Proper and smooth functoriality of the deformation defect
statement:
Fix the algebraically closed field $k$ and finite coefficient ring $A=A_{E,n}$ of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]. Use the specialization datum of [def-trf-deformation-specialization] and the Rees deformation of [lem-trf-dnc-functorial-geometry]. Let $X,X'$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], and write $z:Z\hookrightarrow N_{Z/X}$ for the zero section. For $M\in D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes], put
$$C_{X,Z}(M)=\operatorname{cone}(z^*\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde X_Z}M\to i^*M),$$
using the canonical zero-section map, defined as follows. Cones and triangulated functors are as in [def-weil-triangulated-category], computed on the functorial derived models of [lem-trf-nearby-cycle-finiteness-exchange]. The closed immersion $i$ maps the pair $(Z,Z)$ to $(X,Z)$, so it has the lift $\widetilde i:Z_D\hookrightarrow\widetilde X_Z$ of [lem-trf-dnc-functorial-geometry], whose special fibre is $z$. The canonical zero-section map is the composite
$$z^*\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde X_Z}M\xrightarrow{\mathrm{BC}^*}\operatorname{sp}_{Z_D}i^*M\xrightarrow{\theta^{-1}}i^*M,$$
where $\mathrm{BC}^*$ is the base-change map of [def-trf-deformation-specialization] for $\widetilde i$ and $\theta:N\to\operatorname{sp}_{Z_D}N$ is the nearby-cycle unit of the constant lift $Z_D$. Part of the assertion is that $\theta$ is an isomorphism for every $N\in D^b_c(Z_{\mathrm{et}},A)$. Let $h:X'\to X$ be a $k$-morphism, $Z'=h^{-1}Z$ scheme-theoretically, and $h_Z:Z'\to Z$ its restriction. If $h$ is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], then for every $M'\in D^b_c(X'_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ there is a canonical isomorphism
$$C_{X,Z}(Rh_*M')\cong Rh_{Z*}C_{X',Z'}(M').$$
If $h$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], then
$$C_{X',Z'}(h^*M)\cong h_Z^*C_{X,Z}(M).$$
These comparisons are natural in the complexes and compatible with composition, localization triangles, and restriction to open subsets. The defect construction is triangulated. For extension by zero on the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero] and the complementary open immersion $j:X\setminus Z\hookrightarrow X$, the localization morphism $C_{X,Z}(j_!j^*M)\to C_{X,Z}(M)$ is an isomorphism. For every $N\in D^b_c(Z_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ one has $C_{X,Z}(i_*N)=0$.

source.place: Lemma 3.2.1(a)--(b), using Proposition 1.4.2 equation (1.8) and Lemma 1.4.3(e); §3.2.2(I) and the triangulated reduction in Claim 3.2.3; the constant-family unit of §1.3.3(a) and Remark 3.2.5

proof.text: First establish the constant-family unit without using zero-section invariance. Write $B=D^{\rm sh}$ and $g:\bar\eta\to B$. On $B$ the unit $\mathbf F_\ell\to Rg_*\mathbf F_\ell$, restricted to the closed point, is the identity of $\mathbf F_\ell$. Indeed the strictly henselian sections--stalk isomorphism and exactness of geometric stalks make sections on $B$ exact. For an injective resolution $I$ of $\mathbf F_\ell$ on $\bar\eta$, $\Gamma(B,g_*I)=\Gamma(\bar\eta,I)$; exact sections on $B$ therefore compute the derived closed stalk. Hence closed-stalk cohomology of $Rg_*\mathbf F_\ell$ equals $H^*(\bar\eta,\mathbf F_\ell)$, which is $\mathbf F_\ell$ in degree zero and zero otherwise. The unit sends a constant section to that same section. These statements apply since $B$ is strictly henselian and $\bar\eta$ is separably closed.

Let $T$ be separated finite type over $k$ and $G$ a sheaf of $\mathbf F_\ell$-modules on $T_{\rm et}$. Apply the punctual derived base-change theorem with $K=k$, $n=\ell$, $X=T$, $S'=B$, $T$ in its notation equal to $\bar\eta$, $E=G$ and $F=\mathbf F_\ell$. The map $g$ is qcqs: it is an affine field extension followed by the principal generic open of the trait. The theorem imposes no finite-type hypothesis on $B$ or $\bar\eta$. A sheaf of vector spaces has Tor amplitude $[0,0]$: tensor is exact at every geometric stalk, since vector spaces are free; exact monoidal stalks and enough points detect that exactness. Thus its lower Tor bound hypothesis holds. Pulling its isomorphism back to the closed fibre, step 1 identifies its source with $G$ and its target with $\operatorname{sp}_{T_D}G$. Its counit-adjoint description identifies this map with the nearby-cycle unit: adjunction sends it to the identity on the geometric generic pullback of $G$. Hence that unit is invertible for $G$.

source.place: Tag 0F1J, lemma-punctual-base-change-upgrade; used to supply the constant-family assertion of Varshavsky Remark 3.2.5

proof.text: Choose $r\geq1$ with $\ell^r A=0$. For a constructible $A$-module sheaf $G$, its underlying abelian sheaf has the finite filtration $G\supseteq\ell G\supseteq\cdots\supseteq\ell^rG=0$. The constructible Serre theorem keeps all images and quotients constructible. Each quotient is an $\mathbf F_\ell$-sheaf. Apply step 2 and the unit-compatible module/abelian comparison for $\Lambda=\mathbf F_\ell$ to obtain its underlying abelian unit isomorphism. The unit is a natural transformation between exact derived functors. Each short exact filtration sequence therefore gives a morphism of distinguished triangles; induction gives the unit isomorphism for $G$ after forgetting coefficients. Apply that comparison again for $\Lambda=A$. Exact coefficient forgetting commutes with inverse image and detects zero cohomology, so the $A$-linear unit is an isomorphism. Finally finite induction on the truncation triangles of a bounded complex gives $\theta_N:N\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{sp}_{T_D}N$ for every bounded constructible $A$-complex $N$. No finite Tor condition on $N$ is used.

source.place: Remark 3.2.5, extension from prime coefficients by a finite filtration and from sheaves by truncations

proof.text: The Rees construction supplies the lift $\widetilde h$ for $Z'=h^{-1}Z$. If $h$ is proper, its factorization through the closed immersion $\widetilde X'_{Z'}\hookrightarrow\widetilde X_Z\times_X X'$ makes $\widetilde h$ proper, by proper base change and composition. Its special-fibre square with $z:Z\hookrightarrow N_{Z/X}$ is Cartesian, because the inverse image of $Z$ is exactly $Z'$. The square of $h$ with $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ is Cartesian by the definition of $Z'$.

If $h$ is smooth it is flat. On affine charts $R\to B$ of $h$, with $J=IB$, tensoring $I^m\hookrightarrow R$ by $B$ is injective with image $J^m$. The extended Rees algebra has coefficient $I^m$ at $t^{-m}$ for $m>0$ and coefficient $R$ at nonnegative powers of $t$. Consequently its tensor with $B$ has exactly the coefficients $J^m$ and $B$ of the source Rees algebra; the natural comparison is an isomorphism. The equality respects multiplication and localization at $k[t]\setminus(t)$, so these canonical affine comparisons glue. Thus $\widetilde X'_{Z'}=\widetilde X_Z\times_X X'$, and $\widetilde h$ is smooth by smooth base-change permanence. This proves precisely the flat clause of Varshavsky 1.4.3(c) needed in (e), using tensor exactness rather than assuming the closed immersion of step 4 is always an isomorphism.

Put $P_{X,Z}=z^*\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde X_Z}$ and $Q_{X,Z}=i^*$. Define $\alpha:P_{X,Z}\to Q_{X,Z}$ to be the exchange $\mathrm{BC}^*$ for $\widetilde i$ followed by $\theta^{-1}$ from step 3. Exact inverse images and nearby-cycle exactness make $P$ and $Q$ exact; geometric generic pullback preserves constructibility, and nearby-cycle finiteness puts $P(M)$ in $D^b_c(Z_{\rm et},A)$. The Serre theorem and the cohomology sequence keep their cones bounded constructible. The inverse $\theta^{-1}$ exists only in the derived category, not as a map of models. So take $C(M)=\operatorname{Cone}(\mathrm{BC}^*_M)$ of the exchange $\mathrm{BC}^*_M:P(M)\to\operatorname{sp}_{Z_D}i^*M$, on the functorial derived models supplied by the nearby-cycle exchange node. The natural isomorphism $\theta_{i^*M}:i^*M\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{sp}_{Z_D}i^*M$ of step 3 gives an isomorphism from the triangle $P(M)\xrightarrow{\alpha_M}i^*M\xrightarrow{v\theta}C(M)\to P(M)[1]$ to the cone triangle of $\mathrm{BC}^*_M$. Here $v$ is the cone triangle's second arrow. By TR1 the first triangle is distinguished, so $C(M)$ is a cone of $\alpha_M$, natural in $M$. The node's assertion on cones of exchange transformations gives distinguished triangles of these cones for every distinguished triangle of inputs, including their connecting maps. Naturality of $\theta$ carries this over to the $\alpha$-triangles. Thus $C$ is a triangulated functor. This uses the specified models; a functorial cone is not inferred from the triangulated axioms alone. In steps 8--10, a commuting square of $\alpha$-arrows, multiplied by the corresponding $\theta$, is a commuting square of $\mathrm{BC}^*$-arrows; the induced maps of cones are taken there.

source.place: Equation (1.8), definition at the start of §3, and triangulated assertion in Claim 3.2.3

proof.text:
Suppose $h$ proper, and put $h_0:N_{Z'/X'}\to N_{Z/X}$. Proper base change along $X_{\bar\eta}\to X$ identifies $(Rh_*M')_{\bar\eta}$ with $Rh_{\bar\eta*}(M'_{\bar\eta})$. The proper nearby exchange for $\widetilde h$, then proper base change in the zero-section square of step 4, give isomorphisms
$$P_{X,Z}Rh_*M'\xrightarrow{\sim}z^*Rh_{0*}\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde X'_{Z'}}M'\xrightarrow{\sim}Rh_{Z*}P_{X',Z'}M'.$$
Ordinary proper base change in the original closed square gives $Q_{X,Z}Rh_*M'\xrightarrow{\sim}Rh_{Z*}Q_{X',Z'}M'$. Geometric generic pullback is exact and preserves constructibility, so the nearby exchange has bounded constructible input. All coefficients are torsion; $Rh_*M'$ is bounded constructible by finite-type-over-a-field constructibility, and the same assertion and nearby-cycle finiteness cover the other terms. The proper base-change theorem applies even to bounded-below intermediate nearby direct images, without an extra finite Tor hypothesis.

The endpoint isomorphisms in step 7 form a commuting square whose horizontal arrows are $\alpha_{Rh_*M'}$ and $Rh_{Z*}\alpha_{M'}$. To check the map, before inserting $\theta^{-1}$ paste the ordinary inverse-image exchange for the closed lift $\widetilde i$ with the direct-image exchange for $\widetilde h$. Their outer rectangle is the same for $\widetilde h\widetilde i'=\widetilde i h_{Z,D}$. The mate-pasting identities identify the two composites. The nearby-unit compatibility says that the analogous constant-lift comparison sends $\theta_{Rh_{Z*}N}$ to $Rh_{Z*}\theta_N$, after ordinary proper base change; invert these units using step 3. This yields exactly the asserted square for $\alpha$, including its direction. Taking its cone on the models of step 6, and using exactness of $Rh_{Z*}$, gives
$$C_{X,Z}(Rh_*M')\xrightarrow{\sim}Rh_{Z*}C_{X',Z'}(M').$$

source.place: Lemma 3.2.1(a), compatibility with the canonical map (1.8) expanded

proof.text:
Suppose $h$ smooth. Step 5 allows the smooth nearby exchange, giving
$$h_Z^*P_{X,Z}M=z'^*h_0^*\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde X_Z}M\xrightarrow{\sim}P_{X',Z'}h^*M.$$
The other endpoint is the identity $h_Z^*i^*M=i'^*h^*M$. For the closed lifts, $\widetilde h\widetilde i'=\widetilde i h_{Z,D}$, so composition compatibility of ordinary inverse-image exchanges identifies the composites to $\operatorname{sp}_{Z'_D}i'^*h^*M$. Nearby-unit compatibility identifies $h_Z^*\theta_{i^*M}$ with $\theta_{h_Z^*i^*M}$ under the constant-family exchange. After inserting their inverses this is the commuting square for $h_Z^*\alpha_M$ and $\alpha_{h^*M}$. Exactness of $h_Z^*$ and the functorial cone construction yield $h_Z^*C_{X,Z}(M)\xrightarrow{\sim}C_{X',Z'}(h^*M)$; invert this to obtain the orientation in the statement. Pullback preserves constructible sheaves, and exactness preserves the finite cohomological range, so $h^*M$ remains in the required domain.

All endpoint maps were the adjunction exchanges and their ordinary composition identifications. For composable proper maps the two iterated endpoint comparisons equal the outer comparison by mate pasting; for composable smooth maps the same equality is the composition law for inverse-image exchanges. The nearby-unit equations used in steps 8--9 persist under that pasting. On the specified cone models, maps on cones are induced by the endpoint maps, hence those equalities give composition and identity compatibility for $C$. Naturality in complexes follows in the same way. Applying these maps to a distinguished triangle commutes also with its connecting arrow by the cone/triangle compatibility in step 6. An open immersion is smooth (its restrictions are identities on open charts, satisfying the smooth lifting and presentation conditions), so step 9 gives compatibility with restriction to every open subset and its canonical map. For a proper map restricted over $W\subseteq X$, apply the base-change-of-exchange diagram to the proper squares of step 7 and the open restrictions of their four corners. Its vertical maps are invertible by proper or open base change, so it identifies the restricted endpoint maps with those for $h^{-1}W\to W$. Unit compatibility then does the same for $\alpha$, and taking cones proves compatibility of the proper comparison with open restriction. The module/abelian comparison carries this diagram to constant $A$ coefficients.

source.place: Lemma 3.2.1 and §3.2.2(III), coherence of the canonical comparisons

proof.text:
For the identity closed pair $(Z,Z)$ the ideal is zero, so the Rees algebra is $\mathcal O_{Z_D}$, the normal cone is $Z$ and the closed lift is the identity. Hence its map $\alpha$ is $\theta^{-1}$ and its defect is zero by step 3. Apply step 8 to the proper closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$; its inverse-image centre is all of $Z$. This gives $C_{X,Z}(i_*N)=C_{Z,Z}(N)=0$ (the map $h_Z$ is the identity of $Z$), since closed direct image is exact. Finally the functorial etale localization triangle
$$j_!j^*M\longrightarrow M\longrightarrow i_*i^*M\longrightarrow j_!j^*M[1]$$
becomes a distinguished triangle under $C$ by step 6, with zero third object by the preceding calculation. Its first arrow is therefore an isomorphism. Naturality and compatibility with the connecting map are those of the localization triangle and of step 10. Here the closed and open restrictions are bounded constructible by constructible pullback. Extension by zero is constructible by adjoining the zero stratum $Z$ to the stratification on $U$; exactness and the displayed triangle retain boundedness.
